1.

The appellant/claimant has preferred this misc. appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles
Act, 1988 seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded vide judgment/award dated
01.12.2006 passed by the learned Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Parbatsar in Mac
No.136/2004 whereby the learned Tribunal awarded compensation to tune of Rs.3,29,800/- along
with interest @ 6% per annum towards owing to the injuries [2024:Rj-Jd:34084] (2 of 7)
[Cma-1670/2007] sustained by him in a motor accident which took place on 06.06.2004.

Brief facts of the case are that on 06.06.2004 the appellant/claimant along with other persons was traveling in a Car bearing Registration No. RJ-21-C-5313.

Near Khokhar, Parbatsar a truck bearing registration no. RJ-31-G-4958, being driven negligently and rashly by Respondent No.1-driver, came in front of the car and dashed the car and as a result whereof, the appellant/
claimant sustained injuries.
Subsequent thereto, a charge-sheet came to be filed against the respondent-Driver Jagseer Singh for the offenses under Sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC before the competent Court.

Individual claim petitions were filed by the claimants before the learned MACT,
Parbatsar which were jointly heard.

3. In the claim petition No.136/2004 filed by the appellant/claimant herein, it was averred that he sustained grievous injuries resulting into fracture to elbow of his right hand, fracture toribs for which he had to remain admitted in the hospital.
Further, it was averred in the claim petition that he underwent operation, leaving him permanently disabled.
It was also averred by the appellant/claimant in the claim petition that his disability was assessed as 62% by the Medical Board.
He was aged 30 years at the time of accident and was earning Rs.9,000/- per month from Marble Business.
Thus, the appellant/claimant claimed for compensation jointly against the non-claimants/respondents.

[2024:RJ-JD:34084] (3 of 7) [CMA-1670/2007]
4. Replies were filed by the non-claimants while denying the averments made in the claim petition of the claimant.
The respondent-Insurance Company vide its reply denied the fact of insurance of the truck in question.

5. As per pleadings, the learned Tribunal framed following issues:-

6.

After considering the evidence, documents and hearing all the parties, the learned Judge, MACT Parbatsar decided the claim petition vide a common order dated 01.12.2006, whereby a total compensation of Rs.3,29,800/- was awarded to the appellant/ claimant holding joint liability of the non-claimants/respondents Nos.1 to 3.

Hence, being dissatisfied with the same, the instant misc.
appeal has been preferred by the claimant/appellant seeking enhancement of the compensation.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submits that the findings recorded by the learned Tribunal is contrary to the law [2024:RJ-JD:34084] (4 of 7) [CMA-1670/2007] and facts.
He further submits that the percentage of disability has not been given due consideration.
He also submits that Manoj Kumar vs Jagseer Singh And Ors. ...

the learned Tribunal did not provide adequate compensation with regard to pain, physical and mental agony and other sufferings suffered by the appellant due to the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
He also submits that the learned Tribunal has erred in not awarding any amount towards the future loss of income due to disability sustained by the appellant which reduced his earning capacity.

8. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant also contended that the learned Tribunal has assessed the notional loss by using a unique method wherein Rs.2,000/- was taken as a factor for 1%
disability and multiplied the same with 62% which is the percentage of disability suffered by the appellant/claimant during accident and awarded Rs.1,24,000/- to the claimant/appellant whereas,
the appellant has proved that he incurred Rs.1,88,000/- on medical treatment by producing exhibits on record but the same were not considered by the learned Tribunal.

As the claimant/appellant was engaged in a Marble Business and was earning Rs.9,000/- per month, he was having every likelihood of earning more in future, but the learned Tribunal has seriously erred in awarding compensation to him on a lower side.

In support of his contentions, learned counsel for the appellant/claimant places reliance upon the judgment passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Purushotam Vs. Kayumdeen & Anr. : SBCMA No.1170/2023.

sentences.text: 9. Per contra, learned counsel representing the respondent no. 3/insurance company vehemently opposed the submissions advanced by the learned counsel on behalf of the appellant and urged that the instant misc. appeal deserves to be rejected.
10. I have heard and considered the submissions advanced at Bar and have gone through the impugned award and the original record.

The quantum of compensation as awarded by the learned Tribunal is as follows:-
Simple Injuries: Rs. 3000/-
3 x 1000= 3000/-
Disability (62%) Rs. 1,24,000/-
62 x 2000= 1,24,000/-
Medical Bills Rs. 1,88,000/-
Attendant Charges Rs. 14,800/-
TOTAL Rs. 3,29,800/-
11.

This Court finds that the submission made by t appellant/claimant regarding payment of future prospects, does not have any force, as it is nowhere mentioned in the disability certificate which is available on the record, that permanent disability is caused to the appellant/claimant but the same only mentions disability of 62%.
Furthermore, no material is available on record which goes on to show that there is any loss of income to the appellant/claimant.
Thus, the learned Tribunal is perfectly justified in not awarding any amount under the heads of future prospects and loss of income.

sentences.text: However, the learned tribunal has only awarded Rs.1,88,000/- under the head of medical bills and the same deserves to be enhanced to Rs.2,87,649.52/- as the appellant/claimant placed on record proofs of medical bills and [2024:RJ-JD:34084] (6 of 7) [CMA-1670/2007] expenses which he bore during the time of treatment in the hospital.
Thus, the contention of appellant regarding enhancement of award under the heads of medical bills has sufficient force.

13. Learned counsel for the parties were directed to submit the calculations after this Court arrived at a conclusion that the appellant/claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation looking to the nature of injuries suffered by him and medical expenses incurred by him for his treatment.

Accordingly in light of "Revised Guidelines for Settlement in MACT Cases" issued by the Rajasthan State Legal Services Authority dated 15.04.2021, this Court modifies the quantum of compensation awarded vide the impugned order dated 01.12.2006 by the learned Tribunal as under:-
Hospitalisation for 37 Days: Rs. 22,200/- 37(days) x 600= 22,200/-
Simple Injuries: Rs.97,500/-
3 x 2500= Rs.7,500/-
Grievous Injuries:
1. Fracture of femur bone 2. Fracture of shaft of ulna and radius shaft 45,000+45,000 = Rs.90,000/-
Medical Bills

Attendant Charges(same as awarded by Rs.14,800/-
the learned Tribunal)

Disability (62%) Rs.1,24,000/-
62 x 2000= 1,24,000/-(same as awarded by learned Tribunal)
TOTAL Rs.5,46,150/-
(Less) Already awarded by the learned Rs.3,29,800/-
Tribunal ENHANCED (round figure) Rs.2,16,350/-
14. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed and the amount of compensation payable to the claimants is further enhanced by Rs.2,16,350/- in the terms stated above.
The enhanced amount [2024:RJ-JD:34084] (7 of 7) [CMA-1670/2007] shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of deposit.

The enhanced amount shall be deposited by the respondents/non-claimants with the Tribunal within a period of two months from today failing which, the interest shall stand enhanced @ 7.5% per annum from the date of this order till actual realization.
The award judgment-cum-award dated 01.12.2006 passed by the learned Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Parbatsar in MAC No.136/2004 is modified accordingly.
Any amount already paid by the respondents, shall be adjusted towards the amount finally awarded by this Court.
No order as to costs.
Record be returned to the Tribunal forthwith.
